Images I opened with Read and looked at: storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png, storyboards/page-05.png (numbered PNG; the request hashes the SVG), review/page-04.png, review/page-05.png and review/page-06.png. I did not open the individual 05 panel PNGs.

Script against source: all four text items are verbatim from source PAGE 5. There is no diagnosis or treatment advice, and the stethoscope stays around her neck.

05-1 preview: Ananya is at the left behind the desk, with a closed laptop and an open-hand welcome. Ravi sits down at the right with his bag on the floor by the chair. The balloon is to the right of her face and its short tail points to her mouth, without covering her face. No tablet is visible.

05-2 preview: Ananya's back of head (bun, gold stud, white coat) is at the left foreground. Ravi rubs his neck with his right hand, and the watch is on his left wrist, which rests on his knee. The balloon's tail runs to his mouth. Its lower-left corner sits just above the top of Ananya's back of head, which is a back of head and not a face. Not blocking.

05-3 preview: Ananya leans forward with her hands folded and motion marks beside her head showing a nod. Ravi's back of head and green shoulder are at the right, so screen direction is kept. The closed laptop edge is at the lower left. The caption box sits about 3 px inside the panel's top-left border, so at reading size it nearly merges with the border. It still reads as a caption, so this is cosmetic and not blocking.

05-4 preview: Ananya at the left makes an open-hand gesture, and the balloon's tail clearly reaches her mouth. Ravi at the right shows nod marks, his hands are on his knees and his bag is on the floor.

Each panel has a single text item, so the order follows the grid. The question in 05-1 leads straight to the answer in 05-2, below and to the left, and the caption in 05-3 sits to its right in the same row.
Screen direction holds across all four panels: Ananya on the left and Ravi on the right. Each mid-row panel puts the listener's back of head in the foreground on that same side.
05-3 works as a silent listening beat. The nod marks and the leaning posture are the visible reply to 'tired lately', and the caption comments on it.

transitions.observation: Same consultation room (window with plants, closed laptop) and same costume. The tablet is put away, and Ravi, last seen as 'RAVI · READY', is now in the chair being greeted by name. Cause and effect are clear.
The question 'what brings you in' is answered directly by 'I've been feeling tired lately', with a reverse angle over Ananya's shoulder.
Reverse shot over Ravi's shoulder. Ananya nods and listens, and the caption names the theme without interrupting the exchange.
Back to the two-shot of 05-1. Ananya replies to his concern with shared next steps, and Ravi nods and relaxes, so the consultation closes on that exchange.

From review/page-06.png: the reception desk with the monitor and Meera, and Ravi with his bag back on his shoulder holding his phone. The setting (reception counter, waiting chairs behind) tells the reader he is back at reception after the consultation. There is no caption, but the change of place and person is unambiguous, and the bag is picked up as recorded.

readingReview.comparison:
My image-only order matches the first reader's and the script.
(1) Balloons covering Ananya's face and name label in 05-1 and 05-4: in the art each balloon sits beside her face and does not cover it. The storyboard placeholder label overlap does not carry into the art.
(2) 05-4 speaker ambiguity: resolved. The tail ends at Ananya's mouth, she makes an open-hand gesture, and Ravi has nod marks.
(3) Ravi's balloon over Ananya's side in 05-2: the tail goes clearly to Ravi's mouth, and only her back of head is beneath it. Acceptable.
(4) The 05-3 caption against the border: it sits just inside the border. Cosmetic, noted above.
(5) The thin consultation: the source specifies exactly these four beats, with no diagnosis. The art adds the nod and the leaning-in, which are the visible responses. Acceptable.
(6) 'Technology' with nothing visible: the closed laptop pushed aside in 05-1, 05-2, 05-3 and 05-4, together with the TV and tablet systems on pages 03 and 04, give it a referent. The caption's point is that the tech stays in the background. Acceptable.
No unresolved items.
